newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - July 16.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories Wednesday:
* Calenergy said it began a hostile attempt to buy New York State Electric and Gas Corp.
* Since PepsiCo bought Pizza Hut, KFC and Taco Bell, its restaurant business has more than tripled in size but sales growth has slumped.
* Brazilian stocks plunged 8.5 percent Tuesday as nervousness about the market's astronomical run-up this year edged toward desperation.
* Intel Corp posted profits above analysts forecasts yesterday, while Texas Instruments blew past Wall Street expectations.
* Delta Air Lines and US Airways are about to get new competition in the New York-Washington air shuttle market from Atlantic Coast Airlines.
* The nations biggest banks reported big second quarter gains.
* Kia Motors was effectively placed under bankruptcy protection.
* Stocks continued their march into the record books, bolstered by optimism over corporate earnings.
* Earnings at Merrill Lynch, Pane Webber and Travelers exceeded expectations.
* Savannah Foods plans to merge with the domestic sugar operations of Flo-Sun.
* Consumers spent more freely in June.
* Pfizer earnings rose 16 percent but fell short of expectations.

* Soundscan, a computerized sales tracking system, is preparing a version for books that some publishers hope could bring efficiency to an industry struggling with declingin sales and bloated print runs.
* A judge ruled that KPMG Peat Marwick abused its relationship with an audit client, Stern Stewart.

* Telephone industry executives said they would petition the F.C.C. to resolve a dispute over digital surveillance, contending that the FBI wanted them to develop wiretapping equipment that goes beyond the law.
